classifications.owner: ftCo_Escape spot-dodge tilt-timer gate (open port defect)
classifications.rationale: OPEN PORT DEFECT held as a classification, not an unreconstructible observation. At frame 9793 P3 Falco's PassiveStandF ends and the player presses shield with the left stick already held down-left (recorded lstick x -0.6875, y -0.7125, past the down threshold since 9791). Retail takes GuardOn (178) into Guard (179) and shields for 25 frames; this port takes the vanilla spot-dodge gate in ftCo_80099794 (inlineB0: lstick.y <= ftCommonData x314 AND x671_timer_lstick_tilt_y < x318) and enters Escape (235) instead, with 14 intangible frames and an undepleted shield (60.0 vs 59.72). Leading hypothesis: the down-tilt timer x671 is armed a frame late in this pad profile, so a two-frame-old hold still reads as a fresh smash. The earlier absence-sentinel reading of this residual was wrong: through 9793-9817 the stream publishes decaying shield HP (60.00 -> 53.28 at 0.28/frame), advancing action ids and incrementing instance ids, and animation_index UINT_MAX with state_age -1 is simply how this stream represents every Guard/Entry/Dead row (41 such runs on P3, 33 on P4, all inside the 9,915-row exact prefix); P3 resumes ordinary live rows at 9818 and finishes the game at three stocks. Gameplay resyncs bit-exactly by 9868 (state flags) and 9916 (shield HP); every row from there to 10502 differs only in the global attack-instance counters (instance_id, instance_hit_by, item.instance_id), each off by one because the 25-frame divergence allocated one different id, and that off-by-one is what marks all 710 tail rows mismatched. Ruled out: all 16 combinations of the UCF rollout flags reproduce this identical fingerprint, and msl_ucf_suppress_spotdodge requires mpColl_IsOnPlatform so it cannot fire on the main stage floor. Native and PPC agree on the complete 710-row boundary.

classifications.owner: Dream Land's replaced grOldPupupu blow machine versus the retail blow-timer RNG draw (ledger canonical:slippi-stage-event-publication)
classifications.rationale: Engine-dump probe capture of retail's own RNG stream settles this. Retail's frame 3922 opens with a randi at LR 0x80211648 -- inside grOldPupupu_802113E0's rand_range blow timer -- before efAsync_Dispatch's 0x3EC rotation draw. The hosted build deliberately replaces Dream Land's wind machine with the recorded Slippi direction stream, because the retail timers sample the mid-frame RNG after effect draws that do not exist headlessly; the replacement consumes no RNG. That one-draw phase shift moves the following it_2725_Logic109_DmgDealt HSD_Randi(3) from the stream position returning 0 (the Sheik needle survives into its bounce state) to the neighbouring position returning 2 (the needle is destroyed). Every retail draw for the frame reproduces exactly from the recorded frame seed, including the surviving needle's Randi(8) = 5 bounce speed and its SetupBounce draws. Control: frame 3919 is an identical needle hit with no Whispy draw, and retail's sequence there matches the hosted one draw for draw. Only the needle's own item lanes diverge; every fighter, physics, and shield lane stays exact, and the episode self-heals.

classifications.owner: Fighter_Spaghetti_8006AD10 pressed-input publication across a hitlag boundary
classifications.rationale: Known hosted defect, carried as explicit debt so the replay keeps its coverage and the eventual fix announces itself. Captain Falcon's pummel puts Ness in four frames of hitlag (1383..1386) during which the capture Anim, and therefore ftCommon_GrabMash, does not run, and the recording holds A from 1383 through 1387 so the press edge lands inside that window. The consequence is exactly one spurious 6-point mash trigger: the hosted and retail grab timers agree through frame 1387 (47/46/45 at 1382/1383/1387) and retail then runs +6 ahead (44 at 1388 against 38, 6 at 1408 against 0), so the hosted timer lands on exactly 0.0 at frame 1408 and trips ftCo_CaptureWaitHi_Anim's grab_timer <= 0 gate one frame before the throw. The grab breaks, fn_800DAD18 stops re-anchoring the pair, and the match forks for the remainder. Everything upstream is exact and retail-verified: the seeded timer (60), the standings rank (1), the 1-per-frame decrement and the 6-point mash quantum all match. MEASURED CAUSE: a retail probe at Fighter_Spaghetti_8006AD10's entry shows the held Ness carrying fp+0x2219 = 0x07 (bit 5 clear) and input.x668 = 0 on every frame of the hitlag, while the hosted build has x2219_b5 set and x668 = 0x100 there. The hosted input update is not at fault -- it overwrites x668 to 0 exactly as it should on the first frame the flag clears; the flag and the stale press are established earlier, when the pummel lands. ftCo_Damage.c's capture-partner arm (the `other_fp->input.x668 = other_fp->input.x66C = 0` line, and the `other_fp->x2219_b5 = true` above it) is the site: instrumenting it shows the hosted build reaching that arm at frame 1383 with fp = Ness (the captured fighter, whose victim_gobj points back at the grabber) and other_fp = Captain Falcon, so it clears the GRABBER's pressed mask and sets the GRABBER's hitlag flag while the victim's own x668 and flag are left untouched -- inverted relative to the effect retail produces on the victim. Which fighter drives that arm for a pummel on a held opponent is the thing to settle next. Not patched under a single replay: x668 feeds every CheckInput owner, so the fix needs the full aggregate as its gate. Both backends fork identically at frame 1408 and carry their own snapshots.
